pages.title: Control Plane Worker: Entrypoint, Router, and Route Policies
pages.purpose: How the Cloudflare Worker is wired: fetch/cron/queue entrypoints, the router's declarative route model with authentication and SCM-provider policies, request context, and the composition roots where env.DB may be read.
instructions: Cover env-validation.ts failing loudly on malformed/short AES keys, and src/logger.ts correlation fields.
Document RequestContext: correlation ids, instrumented D1 handle (`db`), BackgroundTasks, principal/authentication provenance separation, and the CORS + x-request-id/x-trace-id header wrapper.

Explain `defineRoute`/RoutePolicy in src/routes/shared.ts: the RouteAuthentication union (public, handler-authenticated, web-service, user, user-or-service, sandbox with getSessionId binding, sandbox fallback) and `supportedScmProviders` gating that returns 501.
Include a Mermaid sequenceDiagram of a request through authenticate → policy enforcement → route handler → DO stub fetch.

Note the eslint guardrail: production code under src must not read `env.DB` directly — only composition roots (router.ts, the DO constructor, cron handlers), each with an inline disable and justification.

Walk through src/index.ts: WebSocket upgrade branch vs. API branch, the `scheduled()` cron dispatch table (image-build scheduler, abandoned-draft sweep, the `* * * * *` automation tick + autofix queue health check), and `queue()` routing between autofix and image-build finalization batches.

pages.title: Data Model and Persistence: D1, DO SQLite, R2, KV, Queues
pages.purpose: Where state lives and why: the D1 shared index (sessions, repos, environments, secrets, image builds, automations, users/auth), per-session SQLite, R2 media, KV caches, and the Queue-backed finalization pattern.
instructions: Call out the derived-state invariant: automation invocation status is never stored, it is derived from child runs by a single shared SQL definition in db/automation-store.ts.

Document the notable D1 tables from control-plane README + db/: session index and session_repositories, environments/environment_repositories/environment_secrets, repo_metadata, repo/global/scoped secrets, image_builds (scope_kind/scope_id, fingerprints, callback-token hash, finalization lease), integration_settings/integration_repo_settings/integration_environment_settings, automations + automation_repositories + automation_environments + automation_invocations + automation_runs, user/identity tables.
Explain the request-scoped DB wrapper (instrumented-d1) and background task port, plus the queue-lease pattern used to move long provider work outside the request-lifetime durability window.
Give an ownership map: which facts live in D1 vs. the session DO SQLite vs. R2 vs. KV, and how the DO is the authoritative per-session store while D1 is the index/registry.
Include an erDiagram of the highest-value entities (session, session_repositories, environment, image_builds, automation, invocation, run).
List Cloudflare bindings from wrangler.jsonc / terraform (SESSION DO, DB D1, REPOS_CACHE KV, MEDIA_BUCKET R2, queues) and the migration workflow via scripts/d1-migrate.sh and terraform/d1/migrations.

pages.title: Sandbox Data Plane: Provider Infra and In-Sandbox Runtime
pages.purpose: How a sandbox is built and what runs inside it: the sandbox-runtime Python package (supervisor, OpenCode server, agent bridge, tools, plugins, credential helper) and the per-vendor infra packages that package it into images/templates.
instructions: Cover modal-infra specifically: app.py Modal app + secrets, sandbox/manager.py lifecycle, sandbox/build_session.py tagged build sandboxes, images/, and web_api.py as the HTTP surface the control plane calls — including ALLOWED_CONTROL_PLANE_HOSTS validation.

Document the agent-facing JS tools (spawn-child, send-child-prompt, get-child-status, cancel-child, slack-notify, upload-media) and the OpenCode plugins (inspect-plugin, codex/xai auth plugins, provider-token-broker) as separate surfaces from the Python modules.
Emphasize the packaging relationship: modal-infra bundles sandbox_runtime source into its function image, and ruff/lint-staged scopes cover these Python packages.
Explain daytona-infra bootstrap/toolchain, e2b-infra build-template.py + e2b.Dockerfile, and opencomputer-infra build-template.ts as template-building packages, distinct from the runtime.
Include a Mermaid component diagram of the in-sandbox process tree (supervisor → opencode server → bridge → control plane).

Map sandbox-runtime/src/sandbox_runtime: entrypoint.py as CLI + composition root, supervisor.py ordering/restart policy (MAX_RESTARTS, backoff, fatal-error reporting), agent_bridge_process.py, opencode_server.py/opencode_client.py, prompt_stream.py, event_forwarder.py buffered forwarding, repository_boot/sync/hooks, tunnel_environment.py `.tunnels.env` boot ordering, code_server/web_terminal/browser_desktop.

pages.title: The Session Durable Object and Its Composition Root
pages.purpose: One session = one Durable Object with SQLite storage: the thin platform adapter, the eager collaborator graph built by createSessionRuntime, internal HTTP routes, alarms, WebSocket hub, and event/message state.
instructions: Cover the WebSocket hub and hibernation: websocket-manager.ts, ws_client_mapping table for reconnect recovery, connection-authenticator, presence/participant services, and event-stream/event-cursor replay.

Describe SessionDO as an adapter only: initSchema + createSessionRuntime + forwarding fetch/webSocket*/alarm; the runtime is rebuilt per activation and `_runtime` is published only after the graph is fully constructed.
Document src/session/contracts.ts SessionInternalPaths as the router↔DO path contract (drift-prevention), and the src/session/http dispatcher/handlers that serve them.
Explain the deliberate eager construction and the fail-fast posture: provider factories throw on misconfigured deployments so every session request fails at init instead of degrading mid-spawn.
Include a Mermaid stateDiagram for sandbox/session status transitions as implemented in session-status-service.ts and the alarm scheduler, plus a component diagram of the composition root.
Note the eslint rule that only durable-object.ts may import components.ts and only src/index.ts may import durable-object.ts.

Summarize session SQLite tables from schema.ts (session, participants, messages, events, artifacts, sandbox, ws_client_mapping) and the repositories in message/event/sandbox/participant-repository.ts.

pages.title: Shared Contracts and Module Boundaries
pages.purpose: The rules that keep eleven packages coherent: @open-inspect/shared as protocol source of truth, import-boundary ESLint rules, knip, complexity linting, and the ADRs that encode them.
instructions: Cover module-boundaries/public-api/type-contracts tests as the executable enforcement of these rules.
Document the canonical correlation contract: trace_id/request_id/session_id/sandbox_id snake_case at every transport boundary and `x-trace-id`/`x-request-id` headers.
Include a small Mermaid flowchart showing shared → control-plane/web/bots dependency and where protocol drift is caught.

List shared's export surface (types/*, auth, service-auth, models, cron, triggers, completion/extractor, logger, cache-store, git, sign-in-provider, slack, pull-request-tool) and the per-submodule import paths that ESLint enforces instead of the root barrel for auth/service-auth names.

Summarize ADR 0002: ClientMessage/ServerMessage/SandboxEvent/SessionState defined in shared; new protocol variants are added in shared first; consumers normalize at boundaries rather than duplicating unions.

Summarize the composition/import bans in eslint.config.js (env.DB only at roots; components.ts only from durable-object.ts; durable-object.ts only from index.ts; web must use app-owned auth/transport seams) and the repo's knip + scripts/lint-complexity.mjs gates.

pages.title: System Overview: Three Tiers and the Package Graph
pages.purpose: The top-level map of Open-Inspect: control plane, data plane, web client, bots, shared contracts, and infra packages — with the dependency/build order and the boundaries between tiers.
instructions: Cross-reference docs/HOW_IT_WORKS.md and packages/control-plane/README.md rather than duplicating their prose wholesale.
Document the tier split (web client / control plane / data plane) plus the three bot workers and the infra template packages, and where each one's code lives.
Explain the single-tenant trust boundary explicitly: one shared SCM App installation, brokered credentials, no per-repo authorization at session create.
Include a Mermaid flowchart of the tiers with the WebSocket chain (client → SessionDO → sandbox bridge → back) as the spine.
Show the package dependency direction: every TS consumer imports `@open-inspect/shared`, which must be built first.

pages.title: Web Client: Next.js BFF, Auth Proxy, and Session UI
pages.purpose: The Next.js 16 / React 19 client as a deliberately thin BFF: signed proxies to the control plane, app-owned auth seams, the session WebSocket transport + reducer, and the settings/session feature areas.
instructions: Document the transport layer: control-plane-transport.ts, control-plane-json-proxy.ts, control-plane-query.ts, browser-api-fetch.ts, settings-proxy.ts, provider-account-proxy.ts, and the eslint bans on raw `fetch` and on `next-auth`/`lib/auth` imports in web code.

Explain the client session state pipeline: use-session-socket / use-session-transport + lib/session-socket reducer, event-log, artifact-metadata, swr-revalidation, and how SSR snapshot + live messages converge.
Include a Mermaid flowchart: browser → Next API route (signed) → control-plane router → SessionDO, and the separate WebSocket path.
Map the route surface (app/(app)/(sidebar), session/new, session/[id], settings, login, api/*) and where hooks and components own behavior.

State the architectural rule: the web app never stores OAuth provider secrets or admission policy; the control plane is the browser-auth authority and web proxies an allowlist of `/api/auth/*` signed with its `sig1` service credential.

pages.title: Authentication, Principals, and Identity
pages.purpose: Who a request is: Better Auth on the control plane, sign-in providers and admission, the principal/authentication-context split, user identity canonicalization and merging, and sandbox/service principals.
instructions: Cover identity enrichment and merging: user_scm_tokens, linked accounts resolved on demand (not used for browser-session auth), identity-claim exchange at sign-in, user-merge store and scripts/merge-split-users.ts.
Define the Principal kinds (user, sandbox, service) and the separate AuthenticationContext evidence, with canonical `users.id` as the application principal.

Document provider enablement and admission rules: complete GitHub or Google credential pairs enable a provider, partial pairs fail closed, Google requires email/domain admission (or explicit unsafe allow-all), GitHub may use usernames or `ALLOWED_GITHUB_ORGS`; `/internal/auth/sign-in-providers` exposes the enabled set.

Explain the authority split: control plane runs exact-pinned Better Auth against D1; web is a BFF forwarding the opaque session cookie; browser resource requests require both the signed `service:web` channel and the cookie.
Include a Mermaid sequenceDiagram of GitHub OAuth sign-in through the web proxy to the control plane and back to a browser session.
Warn that rotation of BROWSER_AUTH_SECRET signs everyone out and orphans stored OAuth credential columns — link to the secrets/rotation page.

pages.title: Automations, Triggers, and the Scheduler
pages.purpose: Unattended session launches: trigger kinds and condition gating, cron scheduling, invocation/run fan-out, dedupe and concurrency, auto-pause, and the scheduler's recovery sweep.
instructions: Cover dedup and concurrency controls: firing-scoped `trigger_key` UNIQUE per automation, `concurrency_key` overlap scopes, webhook API keys and rotation, and exactly-once failure accounting via `failure_counted_at` CAS with auto-pause after consecutive failures.

Describe the trigger registry in shared/src/triggers: schedule, github_event, linear_event, sentry, inbound webhook, slack; source definitions, normalization, condition types and JSONPath filters, and the registry/condition-dedupe helpers.
Document Scheduler.tick responsibilities: recovery sweep of orphaned/timed-out runs plus processing overdue automations, request-driven invocation from routes and SessionDO completion callbacks.

Explain invocation vs. run vs. session: one firing = one invocation, fan-out to one run per repository/environment target, snapshot-of-target at firing time, and derived invocation status rules (skipped/running/completed/failed/partial_failed).
Include a Mermaid stateDiagram for invocation/run lifecycle and a flowchart of the tick path.
Note multi-repo fan-out limits (≤10 combined targets) and repo-scoped single-repo trigger constraints, linking docs/AUTOMATIONS.md and docs/MULTI_REPO_AUTOMATIONS.md.

pages.title: Commit Attribution, Signing, and Pull Requests
pages.purpose: How agent work becomes attributable commits and PRs: per-prompt git identity, signing (SSHSIG/ed25519), the multiple-PR-per-branch model, PR refresh/snapshots, and the manual-PR fallback.
instructions: Cover PR creation authority: user OAuth token when present, shared App fallback returning a manual `pull/new` URL for Slack/Google-origin participants, and the provider abstraction boundary.

Describe the PR model from the control-plane README: one open PR per head branch per repository, force-push-and-reuse with `updated: true`, head-branch resolution falling back to `open-inspect/<session>`, merged/closed branches released, and the `{prNumber, prUrl, state, headBranch, baseBranch, updated}` response.
Document the signing chain: db/commit-signing + routes/commit-signing, auth/openssh-ed25519 and sshsig, and the sandbox-side git_signer/git_signing plus the `gh` wrapper.

Explain the identity contract: control plane resolves the prompting participant and sends an explicit `gitIdentity` mode (`attributed-user` with name/email, or `agent-only`) which the bridge parses without inference.
Include a Mermaid sequenceDiagram of prompt author → git identity → commit/sign → push → create-or-reuse PR.
Note artifact/PR snapshot projections and the pull-request-refresh path clients use.

pages.title: Environments and Multi-Repository Work
pages.purpose: The repository-set model: ordered repositories with per-repo base branches, environment-scoped secrets and integration overrides, prebuild scopes, and how bots route work into environments.
instructions: Cover bot routing into environments: GitHub `defaultEnvironmentId`, Slack keyword routing rules/channel associations/LLM classifier, Linear team/project `environmentId` mappings.
Define an environment as an ordered 1–10 repository set (first = primary) with description, prebuild flag, and Slack channel associations, and contrast it with ad-hoc multi-repo selections.
Describe secret folding for environment-launched sessions (global + environment, not repository) and link to the secrets page.
Document the three-layer resolution chain global → primary-repo → environment for integration settings, and that only `sandbox` and `code-server` accept the environment layer.
Explain how image-build scopes unify `repo` and `environment` under one registry (scope_kind/scope_id, fingerprints) and how spawn matching uses the repository-set fingerprint.
Explain snapshot-at-create semantics: editing or deleting an environment never rewrites an existing session's workspace; the UI shows the deleted-source state.
Include an erDiagram for environments, environment_repositories, environment_secrets, and image_builds scope.

pages.title: Managed Skills and Prompt-Time Skill Resolution
pages.purpose: Reusable agent instructions: skill definitions and content addressing, profiles, global/repo/environment assignments, session revision pinning, and materialization inside the sandbox.
instructions: Cover git import of skills from repositories (skills/git-import.ts, skill-markdown parsing) and limits/validation.
Define the skill data model and content addressing (skills/content-addressing.ts, db/skills.ts, skill-profiles.ts) including revisions and why sessions pin exact revisions.
Document the sandbox side: managed_skills.py client + materializer writing into the OpenCode global skills directory, and prompt-time autocomplete in the web composer.
Explain assignment scopes and the resolution path at session init (session/skill-resolution.ts, routes/skills.ts, routes/session-skills.ts, session-skills store).
Include a Mermaid flowchart: skill authoring/import → assignment scopes → session resolution → pinned revisions → sandbox materialization.
Reference docs/MANAGED_SKILLS.md for user flow; keep this page focused on the code contract.

pages.title: Model Providers, Subscription Accounts, and Token Brokering
pages.purpose: How AI providers are configured, selected, and authenticated: model catalog and reasoning effort, provider accounts with encrypted credentials and defaults, device authorization, and the short-lived access broker sandboxes use.
instructions: Cover session-time selection precedence and legacy scoped OAuth coexistence (session/provider-account-resolution, selection-policy, automation-provider-selection).
Document adapter design in auth/model-provider-account-* (openai/xai adapters, device authorization, broker) and the refresh services (openai/xai token refresh, oauth-refresh-single-flight).

Explain the provider-accounts V1 concepts from provider-accounts.md: provider account, provider credential, provider default, session provider auth, automation provider auth; sessions store account references only, never credentials, and are pinned to their auth mode.
Include a Mermaid sequenceDiagram of device-authorization connect → encrypted store → session select → broker access token.
State the broker endpoint sandboxes use for short-lived access material and the plugins in sandbox-runtime that consume it.

Summarize shared/src/models.ts as the model catalog authority (providers, ids, defaults, validity) plus per-session reasoning-effort validation, and the AVAILABLE_MODELS/OPENAI_MODELS/GROK_MODELS docs as the user-facing view.

pages.title: Sandbox Boot Modes, Snapshots, and Warming
pages.purpose: How a sandbox comes to exist and get to work fast: boot modes, prebuilt images, snapshots/restores, provider capabilities, lifecycle decision logic, circuit breakers, and proactive warming.
instructions: Cover the three warming layers: filesystem snapshots after prompts, prebuilt images rebuilt on a schedule, and typing-triggered proactive warming from the web client; plus the tunnel-URL wait protocol and `.tunnels.env`.

Define the four boot modes (`build`, `fresh`, `repo_image`, `snapshot_restore`) surfaced as OPENINSPECT_BOOT_MODE, and the repository hook contract: setup.sh skipped on prebuilt/snapshot restores and non-fatal for fresh sessions but fatal during image build; start.sh always runs on non-build boots and is strict on failure; SETUP/START timeout defaults.
Document lifecycle/decisions.ts as the pure decision layer (dead-sandbox deny-list, reconnect-blocked statuses, spawn circuit breaker) versus manager.ts side effects.
Explain provider capability flags (snapshots, restore, persistent resume, explicit stop, timeout enforcement) in sandbox/provider.ts and how image-selection + lifecycle decisions consult them.
Include a Mermaid flowchart of the boot-mode decision tree (snapshot? image? fingerprint/runtime-version floor? fresh?).
State the runtime compatibility floor (MIN_COMPATIBLE_RUNTIME_VERSION in image-builds/model.ts) as a hard gate on image reuse.

pages.title: Secrets, Credential Scopes, and Key Rotation
pages.purpose: The encrypted-at-rest surface: three independent key domains, global/repo/environment secret scoping and injection into sandboxes, secret validation, and what rotation actually invalidates.
instructions: Cover the sandbox-side consumption story: no long-lived GITHUB_TOKEN in fresh/prebuilt sandboxes, credential helper brokered short-lived credentials, and the snapshot/image-build fallback exceptions.
Document AES-256-GCM token crypto in auth/crypto.ts plus the strict base64/32-byte validation posture in env-validation.ts (no silent plaintext or AES-128 fallback).

Enumerate the key domains and never treat them as interchangeable: TOKEN_ENCRYPTION_KEY (user_scm_tokens), BROWSER_AUTH_SECRET (browser cookies + user_identities OAuth columns), PROVIDER_ACCOUNTS_ENCRYPTION_KEY (subscription account credentials), REPO_SECRETS_ENCRYPTION_KEY (repo/environment/global secrets).

Explain secret scoping and resolution for a session (global + repo or environment), bulk `.env` paste import, validation caps in secrets-validation.ts, and env injection at spawn time via user-env-resolver/sandbox-env.

For each, state exactly what breaks on rotation and the required migration procedure (including the provider-accounts dual-key decrypt/re-encrypt-and-verify dance and that sessions pinned to lost credentials are unrecoverable).
Reference docs/SECRETS.md and link to the source-control credential-helper page rather than duplicating token tables.

pages.title: Sessions, Participants, and Status
pages.purpose: The session as the unit of work: creation inputs, targets, participants and multiplayer presence, status transitions, archiving/draft expiry, and title/cost projections.
instructions: Cover message queue semantics (durable queueing, MAX_UNFINISHED_PROMPTS, stop execution, terminal-message projection) at concept level, deferring the transport detail to the prompt round-trip workflow.

Define the four session targets (single repo, ad-hoc up-to-10 repositories, environment, no repository) and how exactly one input form is accepted at create (see create-session-input.ts, repository-target.ts, session-create.ts).
Document the status model and reconciliations in session-status-service.ts, archive/unarchive, draft sessions and the abandoned-draft sweep cron.
Explain participants and identity: participant-service/participant-repository, presence indicators, message attribution to the prompting user, public session id latching, and identity enforcement.
Include a Mermaid stateDiagram for session/draft/archive status and a short state table for sandbox status coupling.

pages.title: Integration: GitHub Bot
pages.purpose: GitHub webhooks as a session client: PR auto-review, @mention commands, delivery dedupe, session targeting, and the autofix feedback handoff.
instructions: Cover delivery dedupe via Cloudflare KV keyed by `X-GitHub-Delivery` and the best-effort (eventually consistent) caveat.
Describe session targeting: repository default, `defaultEnvironmentId` metadata override with the containment requirement, model selection, and acknowledgment reactions.
Document the webhook entry (verification, payload schemas), handler split by event, and the two capabilities (auto-review on PR open, comment-triggered actions).
Explain the translator-only design: no PR context fetching, no session reuse, the agent in the sandbox does GitHub interaction with `gh`, and results are posted from the sandbox.
Include a Mermaid sequenceDiagram of webhook → dedupe → session create → prompt → agent posts review, plus the autofix branch.
List the required GitHub App permissions/events and the two-phase Terraform service-binding deployment pattern.
Trace autofix ingress to the control-plane queue and per-repo configuration.

pages.title: Integration: Inbound Webhooks (GitHub, Sentry, Generic)
pages.purpose: The control plane's own webhook surface: GitHub PR lifecycle and workflow events, Sentry alerts, generic authenticated automation webhooks, and Slack event ingress — how payloads normalize, dedupe, and gate session creation.
instructions: Cover pull-request-lifecycle handling (status/label/merge reactions feeding session PR state) and how events reach the scheduler for fan-out.
Document failure semantics: rejected payloads, skipped invocations with skip_reason, and auto-pause after repeated failures.
Enumerate control-plane webhook routes and their auth modes (HMAC/secret verification, per-automation API keys with rotation, Sentry signature verification).
Explain normalization into `AutomationEvent` shapes via shared/src/triggers sources, condition evaluation (JSONPath filters, GitHub conclusion/workflow filters), and trigger-key dedupe.
Include a Mermaid flowchart from inbound payload → verify → normalize → conditions → invocation → runs.

pages.title: Integration: Linear Bot
pages.purpose: Linear as a session client: webhook handling, issue-to-session target resolution, progress activities, and PR linking back to the issue.
instructions: Cover model resolution, plan/start callbacks, and completion/notification posts back into Linear with the resulting PR link.
Document webhook signature verification, event routing in webhook-handler.ts, and the state kept in KV (kv-store) for callbacks.
Explain target resolution: team/project mappings that may name a repository or an `environmentId`, cached resources, and the LLM classifier path for assignments/mentions.
Include a Mermaid sequenceDiagram: Linear webhook → target resolution → session create/prompt → callback → issue comment/activity + PR link.
Note the shared trigger types when Linear events feed automations, and the service-auth call to the control plane.

pages.title: Sandbox Provider Reference
pages.purpose: Comparison of the supported sandbox backends and their capability differences, REST clients, settings, env vars, and image-build adapters.
instructions: Document provider selection configuration (`SANDBOX_PROVIDER`, integration settings layers, per-repo/environment overrides) and required env/binding names per provider from the factories.

Give a capability matrix: snapshots, restore, persistent resume, explicit stop, timeout enforcement, tunnel/port support, and image-build path per provider (Modal, Daytona, E2B, OpenComputer, Vercel).
Link the provider docs and infra packages rather than reproducing setup steps.
Note where a provider is intentionally capability-limited and how lifecycle decisions degrade (deny-list reconnect semantics, image reuse floor).

Summarize each provider's client quirks worth knowing before editing: Modal function/sandbox split, Daytona resume semantics, E2B auto-pause/timeout defaults, OpenComputer template build, Vercel base snapshot bootstrapping.

pages.title: Service-to-Service Authentication (sig1) and Callback Signing
pages.purpose: How the web client and bot workers authenticate to the control plane, and how sandboxes/builders call back: the sig1 signed-request format, per-service credentials, asserted actors, and single-use callback tokens.
instructions: Cover the bots' outbound side (each package's internal-auth.ts plus signedControlPlaneFetch) and how Terraform wires per-service secrets.

Document the control-plane verification side: auth/service/request-authenticator.ts, auth/service/config.ts, callback-signing.ts, and the RouteAuthentication kinds that accept service vs. user vs. sandbox principals.
Explain image-build callback auth: single-use bearer token minted at trigger time, only its HMAC hash stored, and the bound provider session id requirement.

Explain the sig1 format in shared/src/service-auth.ts: canonical request string binding method/path/query/body hash/asserted actor, SERVICE_NAMES, headers, timestamp/nonce grammar, verification failure ordering, and the golden vectors fixture that pins the layout (any change ⇒ new format tag, never an edit).
Include a Mermaid sequenceDiagram of a bot request signed with sig1 and verified by the router.
Note sandbox auth tokens and WebSocket tokens as separate, session-scoped credential kinds; link to the secrets page for encryption-at-rest keys.

pages.title: Integration: Slack Bot
pages.purpose: Slack as a session client: event and interaction handling, target clarification and environment routing, attachments, App Home preferences, and completion notifications back into threads.
instructions: Cover the callback and completion path: session completion notifications, activity status updates, slack-notify tool from the sandbox, and failure/notification semantics.
Describe the worker shape (Hono app, event/interaction/command routes) and its unidirectional service-bound/sig1-authenticated calls to the control plane.
Document prompt attachments (PNG/JPEG/WebP/GIF) intake, forwarding/edited messages, thread context, and per-user model/branch preferences via App Home.
Explain target selection: channel keyword routing rules, channel associations on environments, the LLM classifier over repositories and environments, and target-clarification prompts when ambiguous.
Include a Mermaid sequenceDiagram: Slack event → classifier → control-plane session create → prompt → completion reply.
Note dedupe/idempotency concerns and KV-backed state where used.

pages.title: Source Control Providers and Brokered Git Credentials
pages.purpose: The SCM abstraction: single-provider deployment model, provider interface surface, GitHub/GitLab implementations, and the sandbox git-credential helper that mints short-lived tokens.
instructions: Cover GitHub App token minting (github-app.ts), user OAuth tokens for PRs, and GitLab PAT requirements.

Document the credential helper flow: git in the sandbox calls the helper, helper hits `POST /sessions/:id/scm-credentials` with the sandbox token, response shape with `expires_at_epoch_ms`, and the 401/404/5xx failure meanings.
Include a Mermaid sequenceDiagram of a sandbox git fetch/push authenticated through the brokered helper.
Include the contribution checklist expectations verbatim in summary form (factory case, env resolver, no provider-specific logic in router/session/slack, tests, ADR/docs updates).
Map the SourceControlProvider interface responsibilities (repo listing/access, PR creation, push spec, manual PR URL, credential-helper auth, branch resolution) and where providers live.
State the ADR 0001 model: one provider per deployment selected by `SCM_PROVIDER`, no per-session provider state, unimplemented providers (bitbucket) return explicit 501 on non-public routes.

pages.title: Operations: Local Development and Day-to-Day Commands
pages.purpose: Getting a working loop on your machine: bootstrap, the three setup paths, per-package dev/test/build commands, formatting and hooks, and where local env files must point.
instructions: Document `bash .openinspect/setup.sh` (npm install, build shared, husky hooks, optional Python venv) and why shared is built first.
Include a Mermaid flowchart of the local dev topology (web → local/workerd control plane → real or mocked providers).

Lay out SETUP_GUIDE paths A (web against a dev control plane), B (contribute code), C (deploy your own), including the origin-bound browser-auth caveat that a production control plane cannot authenticate a localhost web app.
List local prerequisites and env files (packages/web/.env.example, packages/modal-infra/.env.example, CONTROL_PLANE_URL/WS URL/SERVICE_AUTH_SECRET) without duplicating every variable.
Mention the contributor workflow expectations: conventional commit prefixes, PR checks, and which CI jobs run for which paths.

Provide the command matrix: build/lint/format/typecheck/knip at root, per-workspace vitest commands, control-plane integration tests, pytest + ruff for Python packages, wrangler/dev-server specifics per package.

pages.title: Operations: Logs, Correlation, and Debugging Playbook
pages.purpose: How to find out what happened: the structured log envelope, canonical correlation fields and boundary conversion, the per-service event catalog, and the log-query tooling.
instructions: Describe scripts/cf-logs.ts usage (Workers Observability Telemetry API, required token/account env vars, --session/--json forms) and how to reproduce locally.
Document the common log envelope, level guidelines, and redaction rules from docs/DEBUGGING_PLAYBOOK.md, and the shared logger implementation each service reuses.

Explain correlation fields (trace_id, request_id, session_id, sandbox_id), camelCase↔snake_case boundary conversion points, and how to join logs across web, control plane, bots, modal-infra, and sandbox runtime.
Include a Mermaid flowchart of a triage decision path keyed by symptom.

Summarize the event catalog by component (router, image-builds, session-do, lifecycle-manager, provider clients; modal api/sandbox/supervisor/bridge/git; slack handler/attachments/callback/classifier) so a reader knows which event names to search.

Walk the debugging scenarios that matter most: missing Slack image, message X never answered, sandbox not connecting, spawn failure, snapshot restore failure, slow spawns — naming the first query for each.

pages.title: Operations: Terraform Deployment and Cloud Wiring
pages.purpose: How the system is deployed and configured: the production Terraform root module split, Cloudflare/Vercel/Modal/Daytona/E2B/OpenComputer wiring, D1 migrations, and the deploy CI workflow.
instructions: Cover the two-phase worker pattern used for service bindings (deploy, then `enable_service_bindings = true`) for the bot workers, and web hosting options (Vercel vs OpenNext on Workers).

Describe the directory contract: modules/ per provider, environments/production split by concern (workers-*.tf per service, web-*, d1.tf, kv.tf, r2.tf, modal/daytona/e2b/opencomputer/vercel, checks.tf, moved.tf), R2 state backend.
Document the D1 migration path (terraform/d1/migrations + scripts/d1-migrate.sh) and the rule that integration tests apply the same migrations.

Explain how configuration reaches the workers: `terraform.tfvars` for secrets/env bindings, generated/persisted encryption keys, service-auth secrets per service, WEB_APP_URL exact-origin requirement, DO/D1/KV/R2/Queue bindings.
Include a Mermaid flowchart or dependency diagram of the deployed resources and their bindings.
Note what .github/workflows/terraform.yml and deploy-web.yml do, and the safe sequence for a schema + code change.

pages.title: Sandbox ↔ Control Plane Protocol
pages.purpose: The contract between the in-sandbox bridge and the SessionDO: WebSocket connect/auth, commands down, events up, acks and buffering, reconnect semantics, and the auxiliary HTTP endpoints a sandbox may call.
instructions: Document the connect handshake: sandbox WebSocket token verification (`/internal/verify-sandbox-token`), the `sandbox` principal kind, and how the bridge authenticates each request with its session-scoped token.

Enumerate downlink commands (prompt, stop, snapshot, git identity per prompt author, tunnel urls, spawn context) and uplink SandboxEvent kinds via sandbox-events handlers in the control plane and event_forwarder/bridge on the sandbox side.

Explain the durability expectations: buffered event forwarder, acks, reconnection behavior, and that losing the sandbox WebSocket does not stop the sandbox (heartbeat check scheduled by the control plane).
Include a Mermaid sequenceDiagram of connect → subscribe → prompt → streamed events → ack → stop/snapshot.
Point out the wire-shape conversion boundary: control-plane camelCase domain types vs. the snake_case runtime payloads (e.g. baseBranch → branch in repository config).

pages.title: Testing: Control-Plane Integration Tests in workerd
pages.purpose: How to write and debug control-plane integration tests: the Miniflare pool, real D1 with Terraform migrations, shared-instance cleanup discipline, helpers, outbound-service stubs, and the Docker harness.
instructions: Cover Dockerfile.test as the containerized harness and the typecheck triple-project setup (src, tsconfig.test.json, test/integration).
Describe outboundService stubbing rules for Modal/OpenAI/xAI endpoints and the `luxon` CJS alias trap that silently skips automations if broken.
Document the migration contract: D1 migrations are read from terraform/d1/migrations and applied via apply-migrations.ts, so schema changes land as migrations, not test fixtures.

Explain `vitest run --config vitest.integration.config.ts`: `cloudflareTest()` plugin, wrangler.jsonc bindings, pinned compatibilityDate/flags matching Terraform, and per-file isolated D1 storage with in-file sharing.
Include a Mermaid flowchart of a test run lifecycle from pool boot to migration apply to assertions.
State the cleanup discipline: shared D1 instance per file requires `cleanD1Tables()` (test/integration/cleanup.ts) in beforeEach/afterEach to avoid cross-test pollution.
Walk the helper API in test/integration/helpers.ts (initSession, queryDO, seedEvents) plus identity-seed and image-build helpers, and `session-do-access.ts` for reaching inside a DO.

pages.title: Testing: Provider, Sandbox, and Bot Coverage Map
pages.purpose: Where the non-control-plane tests live and what they pin: sandbox provider clients and image-build adapters, sandbox-runtime Python suites, per-bot handler tests, and web client tests.
instructions: Cover bot test layout: slack-bot index.test.ts plus per-feature tests, linear-bot webhook-handler and callbacks tests with test-helpers, github-bot separate test/ directory.
Explain web test conventions (co-located .test.ts/.test.tsx with vitest + React testing patterns) and the boundary eslint tests that enforce auth/transport seams.
Give the change→test map so a contributor knows the minimum suite to touch per edit.

Map sandbox provider test files (per-provider tests, provider-factory, lifecycle decisions/manager, image-build adapter tests) and what contract each guards (capabilities, create-bind-launch, error classification).
Note which suites require external mocks/stubs versus real runtime (workerd, pytest-asyncio).

Summarize sandbox-runtime Python coverage areas: bridge SSE/reconnect/push/ack, supervisor lifecycle and monitor, entrypoint build mode and tunnel URLs, git credential helper and signing, diff collector, prompt stream, tool installation, and the node .mjs tests for child-session tools.

pages.title: Testing Strategy: Vitest, workerd, and pytest
pages.purpose: How this repo tests itself: which suite lives where, the unit vs. integration split per package, runtimes and pools, and the CI gates that enforce them.
instructions: Cover non-test CI gates: eslint (with boundary rules), prettier check, knip, typecheck ordering (shared built first), and the custom complexity lint with its own test.
Document Python testing: pytest + pytest-asyncio, conftest/runtime_helpers for sandbox-runtime, and the node .mjs tests for the JS tools; plus `ruff` gates in ci-python.yml.
Explain the vitest workspace (`vitest.workspace.ts` + per-package configs) and how `npm test`/`test:integration`/`test:coverage` fan out across workspaces.

Give the test-location table: control-plane co-located `src/**/*.test.ts` (node env) vs. `test/integration/*.test.ts` (workerd), web/slack-bot/linear-bot co-located, github-bot separate `test/`, modal-infra and sandbox-runtime `tests/test_*.py`.
Include a Mermaid flowchart or table of suite → runtime → command → CI job.
Provide guidance on what to add when changing each area, and the principle of pure decision modules (lifecycle/decisions.ts) enabling dependency-free unit tests.

pages.title: Recipe: Adding or Changing a Sandbox Provider
pages.purpose: The full insertion path for sandbox backends — provider interface, REST client, capabilities, image-build adapter, infra/template package, Terraform wiring, docs, and the tests that must exist.
instructions: Include a Mermaid flowchart of the provider selection path from settings to spawn.
Include the provider docs expectation (docs/E2B_SANDBOX_PROVIDER.md, OPENCOMPUTER_PROVIDER.md, VERCEL_SANDBOX_PROVIDER.md) and integration-settings layering for provider choice.

Lay out the checklist order: implement SandboxProvider + capabilities in src/sandbox/providers, a typed REST client in src/sandbox, register in provider-factory/provider-name, add an image-build adapter, then the infra package (template build) and Terraform module + variables.
List the required tests: provider + factory tests, lifecycle decision tests, integration coverage, and the sandbox-runtime side contract if env vars change.
Point at existing providers as the reference implementations (daytona, e2b, modal, opencomputer, vercel) and note which capability gaps each handles (persistent resume, explicit stop, snapshots).

State the shared conventions every provider must honor: create-bind-launch image-build contract, callback token auth, runtime manifest/version floor, tunnel/port resolution, env-var and secret injection surface, request deadlines and error classification.

pages.title: Workflow: Child Sessions and Parallel Decomposition
pages.purpose: How an agent spawns and coordinates parallel child sessions in separate sandboxes: the tools, the auth relationship, depth/guardrail limits, and status/cancel/follow-up coordination.
instructions: Cover limits and guardrails: depth caps, per-repo settings, and how children get their own branches/sandboxes and PRs.
Describe resumability rules: completed/failed children can resume with a compatible snapshot, cancelled children are terminal, archived children must be unarchived first.

Document the in-sandbox tools (spawn-child, send-child-prompt, get-child-status, cancel-child) and the control-plane routes they call, including how the parent's sandbox token is exchanged for a scoped child operation — never for the child's token.

Explain parent-child state in D1/DO: spawn context, child summary, parent-prompt path, relationship verified twice (D1 and child DO) and attribution of the queued prompt to the child owner with source `agent`.
Include a Mermaid diagram of the parent↔child session tree with the tool calls and DO-to-DO hops.
Note where child activity surfaces in the client timeline.

pages.title: Workflow: Prebuilt Image Build and Queue Finalization
pages.purpose: The provider-neutral prebuild pipeline: trigger sources, dormant build-session binding, callback auth, durable acceptance in D1, Queue finalization (snapshot, artifact persist, supersede, cleanup), and stale recovery.
instructions: Cover the consumption side: image lookup by scope + fingerprint, runtime-version floor, and the per-provider adapters (modal/daytona/e2b/opencomputer/vercel).

Document callback handling: `/image-builds/build-complete` and `/build-failed` public routes authenticated by single-use token (HMAC hash stored), the atomic D1 accept, then a small secret-free command onto the Cloudflare Queue.

Explain the consumer: lease the accepted row, snapshot/checkpoint the provider session, persist the artifact, transition to `ready`/`superseded`, idempotent provider-session cleanup, retries, and why this lives outside the request lifetime.
Explain the create → bind → launch contract every provider follows: control plane creates a dormant provider session, binds its opaque id to the `image_builds` row, then starts the runtime.
Include a Mermaid sequenceDiagram from trigger → build session → callbacks → queue → finalizer → D1 state, plus a status stateDiagram (building/ready/failed/superseded).

Trace trigger paths: schedule/`IMAGE_BUILD_SCHEDULER_CRON`, manual `trigger/repo|environment` routes, toggle-on, and rebuild-policy/fingerprint evaluation (repository set + SHAs) that decides whether a rebuild is needed.

pages.title: End-to-End: From Prompt to Streaming Events
pages.purpose: The canonical control and data flow: a prompt submitted from web, Slack, GitHub, Linear, or an automation travels through the DO queue to the sandbox and back as streamed events and artifacts.
instructions: Cover failure handling at each hop: enqueue contract validation, sandbox not runnable (spawn required), dead-sandbox deny-list, bridge reconnect, buffered event backpressure, session status reconciliation, callback delivery/retry.
Explain queueing and ordering guarantees, stop/cancel semantics, prompt attachments hydration, and the `prompt_queued` → status/event → terminal projection message sequence clients observe.
Include a Mermaid sequenceDiagram covering client, router, SessionDO, sandbox bridge, OpenCode, and the outbound notification path.
Note that correlation ids (trace_id/request_id/session_id/sandbox_id) must be carried across every hop.

Trace the path with real symbols: route (session-prompt.ts / enqueue contract) → SessionDO message-queue → lifecycle ensure-running sandbox → messenger/WebSocket downlink → bridge → OpenCode prompt stream → event_forwarder → sandbox-events processor handlers → event repository → websocket-manager broadcast → web reducer (and Slack/Linear completion callbacks).

pages.title: Workflow: Creating PRs and Consuming Review Feedback (Autofix)
pages.purpose: From finished work to a merged change: PR creation through the SCM provider, push via brokered credentials, and the GitHub review-comment → queue → follow-up prompt autofix loop.
instructions: Cover queue routing (isAutofixQueue vs. image-build finalization on the same worker), health checking, and dedupe/decision outcomes (received/queued/skipped/failed).

Document the autofix path end to end: github-bot ingress of review feedback → `AUTOFIX_QUEUE` → control-plane `queue()` handler → feedback receipt/decision store → follow-up prompt into the originating session → reply back to GitHub.
Explain per-branch PR reuse and force-push semantics, and how multiple repositories in one session produce one PR each.
Include a Mermaid sequenceDiagram of PR creation and a second diagram for the autofix feedback loop through the queue.
Note failure handling: provider errors, missing user OAuth token (manual PR URL), merged/closed branch release, and feedback attach-context race handling.
Trace PR creation: client/tool → `POST /sessions/:id/pr` or sandbox `create-pr` → SessionDO service → provider push spec + user token/App fallback → artifacts and PR snapshots broadcast to clients.

pages.title: Workflow: Creating a Session and Spawning Its Sandbox
pages.purpose: Step-by-step spawn path: session initialization inputs, provider selection, image/snapshot decision, credential and secret injection, repository boot, runtime start, and readiness.
instructions: Cover failure semantics: spawn circuit breaker, failed-but-reconnectable status, timeouts and deadlines (request-deadline), and how warnings reach the client (boot_warnings).

Document what is handed to the sandbox: repository configs in position order, resolved user/environment/repo secrets, tunnel port settings, skills, model/provider auth references, callback/control-plane URLs and the sandbox token.

Explain the decision points: which provider (SANDBOX_PROVIDER + integration settings layering), which image (repo vs environment scope, fingerprint + runtime-version floor), snapshot restore vs fresh clone, and warming shortcuts.
Include a Mermaid flowchart of the spawn decision tree and a sequenceDiagram of create → spawn → ready.
State the provider-capability differences this path must respect rather than assuming Modal behavior.

Walk from `POST /sessions` (and bot/automation equivalents) through initialize.ts → SessionDO creation → spawn-context → SandboxLifecycleManager → provider interface → runtime manifest/env construction.

pages.title: Workflow: WebSocket Subscribe, Reconnect, and Snapshot Handoff
pages.purpose: The real-time channel contract: token issuance, subscribe authentication, the canonical-snapshot-to-stream handoff invariant, presence, and hibernation recovery.
instructions: Cover presence sync/update/leave messages and the interaction with session_status/sandbox_status broadcasts.
Document ws-token issuance (routes/session-ws-token.ts) and connection-authenticator: what evidence a socket must present and how participants are attached.
Explain deliberately excluded data: sandbox credentials never ride snapshots or semantic messages; clients fetch them from `/sessions/:id/sandbox-access` and invalidate on `sandbox_access_changed`.
Explain hibernation and recovery: WebSocket Hibernation API usage, ws_client_mapping persistence, event replay from event-cursor/event-stream, and reconnect convergence behavior.
Include a Mermaid sequenceDiagram of subscribe → snapshot → live stream → disconnect → reconnect, and list the client → server and server → client message types as a table.
Note the ADR follow-up rules (no retained delta log without measured need; no async work between snapshot read and registration).

State the ADR 0003 handoff rule precisely and diagrammatically: finish auth + async enrichment, then final SQLite snapshot read, then send snapshot and register/persist the socket with no await between them.

pages.title: Quickstart — Navigating the Open-Inspect Wiki
pages.purpose: Entry point and task-routing map for the whole wiki: what Open-Inspect is, the three-tier shape, which page to open for a given kind of change, and the repo-wide constraints that apply to almost every edit.
instructions: Do not restate the whole architecture; route readers onward. Keep it navigable, not encyclopedic.
List the monorepo packages in one table with a one-line role each, linking to the architecture page for detail.

Open with a short 'what this system is' paragraph: a single-tenant background coding-agent platform — Cloudflare Workers control plane + Durable Object per session, Python sandbox data plane, Next.js BFF web client, Hono bot workers.

Provide a task-routing table mapping change intents (add a WebSocket message type, add a sandbox provider, change secrets handling, change automation triggers, touch D1 schema, edit the web session UI) to the specific wiki page that covers it.

State the non-negotiable repo constraints: `@open-inspect/shared` must be built first and is the protocol source of truth (ADR 0002); single-tenant security model — no per-user repository access validation; Node.js 22; `npm run build`/`typecheck`/`lint`/`test` are workspace-scoped.
